reference_system.note: The deposit is dehydrated. No DB-derived claim about solvent or ion counts is possible; solvent-side checks are prompt-derived only.

bundle.policy: Fetched from MDDB at scoring time by the evaluator and verified against the sha256 recorded here. It is NEVER staged into the solver workspace: the agent runs MD and the evaluator does all comparison, so the reference cannot leak.

solve_time_network_policy.rationale: The agent must not be able to fetch the reference it is scored against.

analysis_contract.selection: backbone N, CA, C; residue order; N/CA/C order within residue
analysis_contract.superposition: Kabsch fit onto reference.pdb, then 3 iterations onto the running mean
analysis_contract.note: MDDB publishes eigenvalues and projections but NOT eigenvectors. The scorer recomputes the reference subspace under this contract; the published eigenvalues are recorded as a cross-check only (agreement measured at -2.6% to +3.4% on 2026-08-19).

published_eigenvalue_crosscheck.note: Recorded for provenance. The scorer's recomputation is authoritative.

deterministic_checks.note: Heavy atoms are exact; the total carries a small tolerance so a defensible protonation choice is not punished.
MDClaw defaults to opc; TIP3P must be requested explicitly.
Reads the runner's recorded metadata. Kept as a declaration check; elapsed_simulated_time_is_physical is what actually verifies it.

Measures elapsed simulated time from continuously unwrapped solvent displacement instead of trusting the runner's recorded simulation_time_ns. The self-diffusion coefficient is intensive and cannot tell 1 ns from 100 ps; the accumulated displacement is extensive and recovers the true time to within a percent (989 ps measured against 999 ps true, 98 ps against 99 ps, 15 ps against 9 ps). A submission with no bulk solvent is not measurable and fails, which is the correct verdict for an ensemble generated without dynamics.

Scorer-side precondition: the reference's contract atoms must resolve onto the submitted topology by (residue number, atom name). The agent is no longer asked to analyse anything, so agent analysis skill is not measured here; that belongs in an analysis-only task family that runs no MD.

deterministic_checks.null_hypothesis: the submission is no better than what the fold alone predicts: its RMSIP against the reference is drawn from the spread of elastic network models of the same structure, swept over cutoff 7.0-20.0 A
deterministic_checks.decision: pass when the observed RMSIP exceeds every null draw
deterministic_checks.note: Replaces an earlier test against independent uniformly random subspaces. That null was far too weak: measured 2026-08-19, an elastic-network ensemble that ran no dynamics rejected it at z=46 and a run truncated to 10 ps rejected it at z=36. The structure-only null subsumes it, so only this test is a gate. Against this null the same baselines land at z=-0.04 and z=-2.01 and correctly fail, while a real 1 ns run reaches z=4.38.

Not redundant with the subspace test: RMSIP is invariant to the overall scale of the fluctuations, so a trajectory uniformly expanded by 30% (a unit error, say) scores an identical 0.729 while its Rg moves from 1.14 to 1.48 nm. Measured 2026-08-19. This is the only check that constrains compactness at all.

diagnostics.note: Continuous RMSIP against the reference. Recorded, not scored: the agent runs a modern Amber force field while the reference is Parm99, and that force-field sensitivity is uncalibrated. Accumulated values are the calibration set.

Integrated autocorrelation of the leading modes in the reference: PC1 1236 ps, PC2 1081 ps, PC4 1660 ps. One nanosecond therefore contains less than one independent sample along the slowest modes. Any claim about slow collective motion from a 1 ns run is unsupported; this task deliberately tests only that the subspaces are related, not that they agree quantitatively.

categories.prep: System building. Scoreable without running any MD.
categories.md: Simulation. Requires that the run actually happened and explored the right collective directions.
categories.rationale: Reported separately so a failure is attributable. The adversarial baselines make the point: an ANM ensemble and a 10 ps run both score full marks on prep and must fail on md.

references.note: MoDEL dataset citation carried by the MDDB record

scorer_field_map.note: Where each scored quantity actually lives in an MDClaw submission. Established by solving this task with MDClaw on 2026-08-19; a first pass that guessed these paths produced two false FAILs.
scorer_field_map.net_charge: <topo node>/artifacts/amber_metadata.json :: system_net_charge_e (or sum of NonbondedForce particle charges in system.system.xml)
scorer_field_map.contract_atom_mapping: map the reference's 228 contract atoms onto the submission by (residue number, atom name), never by raw atom index: the submitted topology contains solvent and its indexing does not match the reference
scorer_field_map.barostat_caveat: the barostat is added at run time, so it is absent from the topo node's system.xml; read the ensemble from the prod node's metadata, not from that file

reference_solve_20260819.solver: MDClaw 0.6.6 (ff14SB + TIP3P, cubic 15 A, HMR 4 fs, NVT 100 ps + NPT 200 ps, 1 ns NPT)
reference_solve_20260819.interpretation: Subspace DIRECTIONS are recovered (RMSIP 0.729, all 10 canonical correlations above the null 99th percentile) while AMPLITUDES are 2-6x too small, exactly as the effective-sample-size diagnostic predicts for 1 ns. This is why the task scores the H0 rejection and not quantitative agreement.

prompt_policy.principle: State only what cannot be inferred, and nothing about how to analyse.
deliberately_not_stated: chain selection (each entry has one protein chain)
histidine tautomer (the neutral form is standard at pH 7 and the heavy-atom count is tautomer independent)
box shape and padding (not compared against the reference)
side-chain completion (correct practice, and the point of D02)
the analysis contract (the evaluator computes both subspaces itself; numbers the agent reports are never used)
